title: mTLS for API requests and webhook deliveries
summary: Require a client certificate on API requests through a dedicated mTLS endpoint, and have Bird present a client certificate on webhook deliveries.
body_markdown:
Bird introduces mTLS, available on request, for both directions of a connection.


For API requests, add your certificate authority's public certificate in **Workspace settings → mTLS** (or[POST /v1/workspace/mtls-certificate-authorities](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/create-workspace-mtls-certificate-authority) ), then send requests to the new` mtls.<region>.platform.bird.com` endpoint with a client certificate. Run in` evaluating` mode while you move traffic over, then switch to` enforced` so the standard endpoint stops accepting API key and service account requests entirely.


For webhook deliveries, Bird generates a key pair and a certificate signing request under **Webhooks → mTLS** , your certificate authority signs it, and Bird presents the signed certificate whenever your receiver asks for one during the TLS handshake.[POST /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/test](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/test-webhook) now returns a` client_certificate` field (` presented` ,` not_requested` , or` rejected` ) so you can confirm your receiver is checking it correctly before enforcing.


Both directions support certificate revocation checks against a certificate's CRL, and a required subject alternative name for API requests when your certificate authority also issues to other parties. See the[mTLS guide](https://bird.com/docs/guides/mtls) for setup, rotation, and troubleshooting.


Also in this release:


- **WhatsApp templates can set a delivery time-to-live.**` message_send_ttl_seconds` on a template language controls how long WhatsApp keeps trying before dropping an undelivered message, from 30 seconds up to 30 days depending on category. See[Upsert WhatsApp template language](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/upsert-whatsapp-template-language) .
- **Workspace quotas report their type.**[GET /v1/workspace/quotas](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/list-workspace-quotas) now returns` type` (` integer` or` boolean` ) and` label` alongside each quota, so a feature-switch quota no longer reports a misleading` unit` .
- **Callback signing secrets now cover voice sequence webhooks.** Rotating your workspace's signing secret at[POST /v1/webhook-callbacks/rotate-signing-secret](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/rotate-webhook-callback-signing-secret) re-signs both SMS callback URLs and voice sequence webhook requests, which now share one secret.
